clue.text: Star's endless jargon

indicators.note: something endless has had its final part cut away, so the last letter goes

parts.note: the Pole Star; the 's reads as 'is'

explanation.surface: A celebrity keeps talking in impenetrable showbiz jargon.
explanation.walkthrough: The star is Polaris, the Pole Star, minus its last letter. Polari is the cant formerly used by British theatre folk and gay men.
explanation.definitionFit: Polari is a historical slang vocabulary, which makes it a kind of jargon.

clue.text: Neat park runs wild to become common

definitions.note: past participle of partake, in the sense of having shared

indicators.note: running wild means moving without order, so the letters scatter into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A tidy park overrun by wildlife turns into common land.
explanation.definitionFit: Something partaken has been shared among people, held in common rather than kept by one.

clue.text: See graduate right to help up-coming region

parts.note: lo! is an old exclamation meaning see!

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the word is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: An instruction to visit a graduate and help an area on the rise.
explanation.definitionFit: Lombardia is the Italian name of Lombardy, an administrative region of northern Italy around Milan.

clue.text: Appearance in macro lens

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the following words, spanning the gap between them

parts.note: the tail of the first word joined to the start of the second

explanation.surface: A photographer's subject shows up through a close-up lens.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor's appearance in a film or play is the part, or character, they take on.

clue.text: Rapper's four kings

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ..., the possessive of the stage name of the Black Eyed Peas rapper
second meaning: England has had four kings of this name

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a play on the rapper will.i.am with a possessive tacked on; the second is the four monarchs named William.
explanation.definitionFit: William I to William IV make four English kings sharing one first name, so collectively Williams.

clue.text: How people live losing half of life in scandals

indicators.note: losing something means it is taken away from the phrase before

parts.note: people typically live in family groups
the first two of the four letters

explanation.surface: A sociological observation that family life is full of scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Infamies are acts or episodes of public disgrace, much like scandals.

clue.text: Making Roman signal it in distress

indicators.note: being in distress suggests being in a disordered state, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: A Roman soldier flashes a distress signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To Latinise is to give something a Latin, that is Roman, form or character.

clue.text: See 16
US sect start to hunt missing falcons

indicators.note: missing means a letter is absent from the word before
the start of the next word is the single letter in question

parts.note: the Shakers, a religious community in America

explanation.surface: An American religious group sets out hunting but finds no birds of prey.
explanation.definitionFit: Sakers are large falcons of eastern Europe and Asia, prized in falconry.

clue.text: Labour get rather uncertain naming their leaders

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their opening letters, which are named in turn

explanation.surface: The Labour party grows unsure when picking leaders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like the British political party, but it is the definition: hard menial work.
explanation.definitionFit: Grunt work is heavy, unglamorous toil, so a grunt is a slang word for such labour.

clue.text: Rose Walker

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a climbing rose with clusters of small flowers
second meaning: someone who hikes in the countryside

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a person's name, Rose Walker, but splits into a flower and a hiker.
explanation.definitionFit: A rambler is both a vigorous climbing rose variety and a person who goes on long country walks.

clue.text: Loud bravo from behind ship's timber

indicators.note: one letter comes in place of another taken from the following word

parts.note: forte, the musical notation for loud

explanation.surface: A loud cheer comes from the back of the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Loud bravo from behind' as F replacing B in a word for the backside.
explanation.definitionFit: A futtock is one of the curved timbers that form the lower frame of a wooden ship's hull.

clue.text: Open a container

explanation.surface: An instruction to unseal a box or tin.
explanation.definitionFit: A door left ajar is slightly open, so the adjective matches.

clue.text: He suggests instruction to ban child admitting a temperature

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the word for child takes the next letters inside it

parts.note: a minor is a person under age

explanation.surface: A parent proposes forbidding a feverish child from something.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominator puts forward a candidate's name, that is someone who proposes or recommends.

clue.text: Obscure old poem contains publicity nowadays

indicators.note: the word for poem holds the next item within it

explanation.surface: An obscure ancient poem gets modern-day promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: To overspread something is to cover it entirely, which hides or obscures it.

clue.text: I'd even chop vegetable

indicators.note: chopping cuts things up into a new arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the six letters, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A cook is willing to chop up even the greens.
explanation.definitionFit: Endive is a leafy salad plant of the chicory family, eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Playing tricks on footballer dismissed after new gossip

indicators.note: the word for dismissed is placed behind the next two pieces

parts.note: as a batsman is out in cricket

explanation.surface: A footballer is sent off after fresh rumours about him.
explanation.walkthrough: The word order puts 'dismissed' after the new gossip, so its letters come last.
explanation.definitionFit: Messing about with someone means teasing or fooling them, much like playing tricks on them.

clue.text: Endless delay turned into innocent story

indicators.note: going into means being placed inside the following word
turned round means the shortened word is read backwards
without its end, the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: An endless hold-up turns into a tale of an innocent person.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrative is an account of connected events, another word for a story.

clue.text: Spies hold back side of treacle

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it within, so the next word goes inside

parts.note: moles are agents planted inside an organisation

explanation.surface: Spies hold back one side of something sticky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back side' reads as hold back, but it is one phrase, the bottom. In Britain treacle is another name for molasses.
explanation.definitionFit: Molasses is the dark syrup from sugar refining, which British English calls black treacle.

clue.text: Boxed with old underdogs

parts.note: read as under + dogs: a pack of hounds, with the word for old going under it in this down entry

explanation.surface: A boxer fights alongside elderly no-hopers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underdogs' is split: old goes under dogs, the word for old placed beneath in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Something packaged has been wrapped or put in a box for sale or delivery.

clue.text: Continue to film luggage but lose it

definitions.meaning: second meaning: one of the British comedy film series of the 1950s to 1990s
third meaning: a bag small enough to take onto a plane
fourth meaning: make a scene or behave wildly

explanation.walkthrough: Four meanings, not two: the Carry On films were a long-running series of British comedies full of saucy jokes.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase covers persisting, a comedy film, cabin baggage and making an emotional fuss.

clue.text: Lacking wee bit of hair, unadvisedly retired

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing backwards, so the letters are read in the other direction
only a piece of the following words is wanted, taken from within them

parts.note: the letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A bald man unwisely went to bed early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wee' looks like 'small' beside 'bit', but it is urine.
explanation.definitionFit: Anuria is the medical term for the kidneys failing to produce urine.

clue.text: Lower the bottom half of banner outside

indicators.note: being outside means wrapping round the other item
in a down clue the bottom half is the latter half of the word

explanation.surface: Instructions for hanging a banner lower down.
explanation.definitionFit: Nether is an old adjective meaning lower or under, as in the nether regions.

clue.text: Alexander Brown

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a common pet form of this name

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a man's full name, but splits into a nickname and a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandy is a familiar Scottish diminutive of Alexander and also a light brown shade, like sand.

clue.text: Each panel is assembled with brains

indicators.note: assembling puts parts together in a new configuration, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A clever team puts together every panel.
explanation.definitionFit: Encephala is the plural of encephalon, the anatomical term for the brain.

clue.text: Four countries start manoeuvring for island

indicators.note: manoeuvring moves things around, so the letters are shifted into a new order
the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Four nations begin military exercises over an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Corfu is a Greek island in the Ionian Sea.

clue.text: Raise flag

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests hoisting a flag, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To jack something is to lift it with a jack, and a jack is a small national flag flown at a ship's bow.

clue.text: Signpost dismantled

indicators.note: something dismantled is taken to pieces, so the letters can be reassembled differently

parts.note: the word splits in two; its second half is the fodder

explanation.walkthrough: 'Signpost' reads as one word, but splits into the definition and the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A stop sign is a road sign ordering drivers to halt, so this is an example of a sign.

clue.text: Insects shorten performance

indicators.note: a performance puts on a show, a fresh treatment of the material, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Stinging insects bring a show to a premature end.
explanation.definitionFit: Hornets are large wasps, members of the insect order that includes bees and ants.

clue.text: Too caring to take time for treating eyes soundly

definitions.note: cryptic: dotting the i's, eyes standing for the letter i by sound

indicators.note: taking something in means accepting it inside

explanation.surface: An over-attentive carer takes time over eye treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the idiom of dotting the i's: eyes sound like the letter i.
explanation.definitionFit: Dotting i's is putting the dot over each letter i, here punned as treating eyes.

clue.text: Most like a ball to start off buffet during break

indicators.note: something happening during another thing sits within it
with its start taken off, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: to buffet is to batter or pound

explanation.surface: A rotund guest attacks the buffet at the interval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buffet' tempts as a spread of food; here it is the verb to strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball is perfectly round, so the thing most like one is the roundest.

clue.text: Add a couple of pages conclusion

parts.note: pp is the abbreviation for pages

explanation.surface: A writer adds a short couple of pages as an ending.
explanation.definitionFit: To append is to attach something at the end, which means to add it.
